data.name: Kalayanth
data.gender_notes: Kalayanth is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Kala’ meaning time and ‘Yanth’ meaning lord or ruler. This name signifies the ruler or god of time. The name Kalayanth carries the meaning “God of Time” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kalayanth usually hope their child will grow to embody god of time and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the eternal flow of time and the role of the divine in shaping our lives.
data.etymology: Kalayanth belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Time.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kalayanth total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kalayanth" carries deep cultural significance in Hindu tradition, symbolizing the power and control of time. In Hindu mythology, various gods and goddesses are associated with different aspects of time, each with their significance. Lord Shiva, as a ruling deity of time, is denoted as ‘Kalahasta’ or ‘Kalabhairava.’ The name ‘Kalayanth’ echoes this association, underlining the cultural richness and depth of the Hindu tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Kalayanth" holds great significance as it relates to the divine deity in charge of time, reminding us of the transient nature of all worldly possessions. This name inspires us to cherish the present moment, seeking connection with our higher selves and the divine entity who governs all existence. By acknowledging the passage of time and its connection to the divine, we can cultivate a deeper sense of spiritual grounding, appreciation for life, and an increased ability to navigate the challenges and tantalizing rewards of each moment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kalayanth: Goddess of Time and Change. Her name signifies the eternal flux of life, embodied in the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth. She grants the wisdom to embrace change and find joy in the ever-evolving journey of life.

historical_references.reference: Kalayan or Kalayantha Maharaja was the last king of the ancient Pandyan kingdom in South India which was famous for its rich art and culture in the 13th century AD.

Kalayan or Kalayantha Perumal was a popular name for Lord Vishnu in the medieval period in South India. The name is believed to have been derived from the Sanskrit words 'Kala' (time) and 'Yantha' (support) meaning 'the one who supports the cycle of time'.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Kalayanth' is derived from the Hindu mythology and is associated with the God of Time, Kala. In modern context, this name is popularly used in various trends related to Astrology, Spirituality, and Folklore. On Twitter, several hashtags like #KalayanthAstrology and #KalayanthQuotes are used to spread astrological knowledge and inspirational quotes. The name 'Kalayanth' is often used in a modern, secular context to represent wisdom, time, and spirituality.
